tagline: Three times over the Divide, by way of the silver towns.
intro: Up from Minturn, US 24 climbs past the Eagle River, crosses Tennessee Pass and comes down into Leadville, the old silver town at better than 10,000 feet. Ringed by fourteeners, it occupies the lowlands. South of town Mount Elbert and Mount Massive, the two highest peaks in the Rockies, stand side by side.

From Leadville the byway crosses the Continental Divide twice more. One branch traces the Arkansas River nearly to its source near Fremont Pass. The other runs by Twin Lakes and climbs from 9,200 feet to 12,095 at Independence Pass before dropping into Aspen.

moments.title: Gilman
moments.text: The remnants of a lead and zinc town show along the highway curves, on a 600-foot cliff above the Eagle River. It was abandoned in 1984 and is off limits.

moments.title: Climax
moments.text: The company town at Fremont Pass was razed in 1962 to make room for the molybdenum mine and its houses were hauled to Leadville. The post office carried on until 1974.

moments.title: Independence Pass
moments.text: Prospectors crossed here on July 4, 1879, and named it for the day. An overlook near the top looks over tundra above treeline and east to Mount Elbert.

practical: Independence Pass on CO 82 is closed from October to May.
